es.title: Lorca transforma la lectura en creación con un proyecto que ha involucrado a más de 2.700 vecinos
es.description: La Red Municipal de Bibliotecas de Lorca ha concluido el proyecto “Leer, comprender y crear: La lectura, una reacción en cadena”, una iniciativa de fomento de la lectura que ha reunido a 2.747 participantes de todas las edades en el casco urbano y en las pedanías. La concejal de Educación, Rosa Medina, ha resaltado el éxito de esta propuesta enfocada a estimular la creación individual y colectiva a partir de las páginas leídas. En total se han desarrollado 27 actividades diferentes distribuidas en 99 sesiones de trabajo adaptadas a todos los rangos de edad. La programación ha destinado 14 actividades al público infantil o familiar con 1.111 niños, ocho propuestas al ámbito juvenil en el marco del programa 8Días JL con 1.063 jóvenes, y cinco actividades para adultos con 573 participantes. Fruto de este proceso creativo, los asistentes han elaborado una radionovela, un cortometraje con textos, microrrelatos, poemas, cuadernos de viaje, murales y láminas. La edil ha detallado que "el proyecto ha invitado a los participantes a ir más allá de la lectura: comprender los textos, reinterpretarlos y convertirlos en nuevas creaciones", añadiendo además que "queremos que las bibliotecas sean espacios donde leer despierte ideas y anime a los lorquinos a crear y compartir". Medina ha agradecido la implicación de los centros educativos y el entusiasmo del público, "que demuestra que las bibliotecas municipales son lugares de encuentro y aprendizaje para todas las edades". La red de bibliotecas entidad ha publicado un vídeo resumen de la iniciativa en su de YouTube. La iniciativa ha dispuesto de una subvención parcial concedida por el Ministerio de Cultura dentro de la convocatoria para la promoción de la lectura y las letras españolas de 2025, complementada con una aportación municipal de 10.000 euros.

es.title: El AVE abre una nueva puerta en Almería: así cambiará el entorno de la antigua estación tras el soterramiento
es.description: Almería se prepara para cambiar de panorámica con la llegada de la Alta Velocidad, prevista en 2030. El soterramiento de las vías no solo permitirá que el AVE entre en la capital, sino que abrirá la puerta a una transformación urbana de calado en uno de los espacios más céntricos de la ciudad. La antigua Estación de Ferrocarril, los terrenos que quedarán liberados y su conexión con el Cable Inglés y el Parque de la Estación conforman un ámbito que el Ayuntamiento almeriense quiere convertir en una de las nuevas centralidades.La alcaldesa, María del Mar Vázquez, ha definido ese entorno como «la nueva puerta de Almería» , por donde «va a venir el AVE, por donde van a venir turistas, por donde va a venir inversión». El Consistorio ha presentado un avance de anteproyecto para recuperar la antigua estación como espacio cultural, turístico, de restauración y encuentro, mientras ha abierto también el debate sobre el futuro de los aproximadamente 32.000 metros cuadrados que quedarán liberados por el soterramiento.La propuesta municipal llega después de décadas en las que ese ámbito ha estado ligado a distintos proyectos urbanísticos. Ahora se quiere modificar el planeamiento y reducir la edificabilidad prevista , con una de las alternativas que contempla un 29,24% menos de edificabilidad y reduce el máximo de viviendas de 1.130 a 944. La opción preferida por el equipo de gobierno mantiene vivienda protegida, usos terciarios, espacios libres y zonas verdes, con edificaciones aisladas de hasta diez plantas en determinadas parcelas.«Cuando hace casi 30 años se diseñó el planeamiento que hoy traemos, la realidad de Almería era otra. Nuestra ciudad ha cambiado, nuestras necesidades han cambiado y nuestra forma de entender el urbanismo, también. Hoy no se trata de construir por construir , ni de seguir la inercia del pasado. Se trata de ordenar mejor», ha defendido Vázquez hace unos días.María del Mar Vázquez durante la presentación del nuevo proyecto de uso para la antigua estación de tren ABCLa otra gran pieza es el edificio histórico de la estación, propiedad de Adif. El Ayuntamiento quiere utilizarlo como un gran contenedor cultural , respetando su protección patrimonial y con una intervención «poco invasiva». La planta baja albergaría un espacio central polivalente, sala de proyecciones, galerías culturales, zonas expositivas y restauración, además de recuperar el antiguo andén como espacio cultural y terraza cubierta. En la planta superior se plantea una sala multiusos y un Centro de Interpretación Ferroviaria dedicado a explicar el papel del ferrocarril en la historia económica, social y urbana de Almería y su provincia.La propuesta también contempla aprovechar los espacios exteriores y la azotea para usos vinculados a la restauración . La idea es que el inmueble deje de ser un espacio cerrado o limitado a su función ferroviaria y pase a formar parte de la vida cotidiana de la ciudad.«Pensamos que la estación de ferrocarril es de las más bonitas de España . Es un monumento que no puede quedarse solo para uso ferroviario», ha señalado la alcaldesa, que ha comparado su futuro con el de otros elementos patrimoniales de la capital como el Cable Inglés, recientemente restaurado y de uso turístico.El proyecto incluye además una transformación del espacio situado a espaldas de la estación, actualmente ocupado por instalaciones provisionales relacionadas con la estación de autobuses. Así se estudia convertirlo en una zona verde para pasear que conecte con el Parque de la Estación y el Cable Inglés, creando un recorrido urbano entre dos de los principales elementos patrimoniales de este frente de la ciudad.Edificio de la antigua estación de ferrocarril de Almería ABCUn nuevo escenario urbanísticoEl debate sobre los suelos liberados gira ahora en torno a qué ciudad quiere construir Almería alrededor de la futura llegada del AVE . La alternativa municipal mantiene una importante capacidad residencial, con un 15% de vivienda protegida, pero incorpora también espacios libres y parcelas de uso terciario.La alcaldesa ha descartado expresamente recuperar el modelo de grandes torres que contemplaba el planeamiento anterior. «Lo que tenemos claro es que no queremos torres y queremos proponer qué es lo que necesita la ciudad», ha afirmado.Por su parte, el subdelegado del Gobierno en Almería, José María Martín, ha señalado que el Ministerio de Transportes mantiene su «voluntad de escuchar y atender» la propuesta municipal sobre estos terrenos. Martín ha recordado que «el diseño urbanístico de una ciudad corresponde al ayuntamiento» y que no es competencia de otra institución, aunque ha insistido en que «esa voluntad de acuerdo siempre ha existido».Desde la oposición en el gobierno municipal, la portavoz municipal socialista, Fátima Herrera, ha reclamado que los terrenos liberados se destinen «prioritariamente a crear un gran espacio verde» y a «vivienda protegida y asequible» . Herrera considera que la discusión llega con un «retraso difícil de justificar» y sostiene que estos suelos deben responder a dos necesidades de la ciudad: incrementar las zonas verdes y facilitar el acceso a una vivienda asequible.El Ayuntamiento insiste en que su propuesta es solo un punto de partida. «Todavía no somos capaces de dimensionar completamente la trascendencia que va a tener para la ciudad y para todo este entorno la llegada de la Alta Velocidad», ha señalado. El reto empieza precisamente cuando desaparezcan las vías en superficie y Almería tenga que decidir qué hacer con el espacio que queda detrás de ellas.

pl.title: Skarbówka: Zakup okularów i soczewek kontaktowych można odliczyć w PIT gdy jest orzeczenie o niepełnosprawności – nie tylko dotyczące wzroku

pl.title: Dlaczego lekarze leczą dożywotnio bez weryfikacji kwalifikacji? Dr Rakasz: potrzebny system rewalidacji lekarzy. Co 5 lat kompleksowa ocena i przedłużenie albo wstrzymanie uprawnień
pl.description: Aktualnie w Polsce praktycznie nie funkcjonuje efektywny system rewalidacji lekarzy – czyli okresowej weryfikacji uprawnień i kompetencji). Po uzyskaniu prawa wykonywania zawodu lekarze nie podlegają regularnej ocenie jakości swojej pracy ani obowiązkowej recertyfikacji. Choć formalnie istnieje obowiązek ustawicznego kształcenia i zbierania tzw. punktów edukacyjnych, to w praktyce nikt tego nie egzekwuje. W rezultacie – jak alarmują eksperci – dziesiątki, a nawet setki polskich lekarzy od lat nie uczestniczyły w żadnych szkoleniach czy konferencjach, prowadząc praktykę medyczną na poziomie sprzed kilkudziesięciu lat. Taki stan rzeczy sprawia, że spadek kompetencji lub braki w aktualnej wiedzy często wychodzą na jaw dopiero przy łóżku pacjentów, narażając ich zdrowie i życie - pisze dr n. med. Łukasz Rakasz, Ordynator Oddziału Neurochirurgii Dziecięcej w Szpitalu Dziecięcym im. prof. dr. med. Jana Bogdanowicza w Warszawie.

gr.title: Το τρίγωνο της ναυτιλίας: Καύσιμα, λιμάνια, ναυπηγεία με φόντο τη νέα ατζέντα των Βρυξελλών
gr.description: Από τη μια το κόστος της ενέργειας που πιέζει την ακτοπλοια, από την άλλη η επιτάχυνση του ΥΝΑΝΠ για ανάπτυξη στα λιμάνια , με τις Βρυξέλλες να καθορίζουν ολο και περισσότερο τους κανόνες του παιχνιδιού με είσοδο των ελληνικών ναυπηγείων στη Waterborne Καύσιμα. Λιμάνια. Ναυπηγεία. Τρεις πλευρές ενός τριγώνου και στο κέντρο η ελληνική ναυτιλία . Η μια πλευρά πιέζει το κόστος λειτουργίας με την άνοδο του πετρελαίου και τις ευρύτερες πληθωριστικές πιέσεις, η δεύτερη στρέφεται σε επενδύσεις και υποδομές για την ασφάλεια και έναν πιο αποδοτικό ρόλο στα λιμάνια και η τρίτη φέρνει την πρόκληση της επόμενης ημέρας στην τεχνολογία της νέας γενιάς πλοίων. Το κοινό ερώτημα: Πόσο έτοιμη είναι τελικά η ελληνική θαλάσσια οικονομία απέναντι στο διεθνή ανταγωνισμό και κυρίως του ασιατικού, την ώρα που η Ευρώπη προσπαθεί να αλλάξει τεχνολογικά τον ευρωπαϊκό στόλο; Α κτοπλοΐα: Εκρηκτική άνοδος στο λειτουργικό κόστος λόγω των καυσίμων και έλλειψη προσωπικού ανησυχεί τον ΣΕΕΝ Στο μέτωπο της ακτοπλοϊας οι κίνδυνοι έρχονται από δυο μεριές: η αύξηση κόστους ενέργειας πιέζει ασφυκτικά τον κλάδο και η έλλειψη προσωπικού στα επιβατικά και εμπορευματικά πλοία φέρνει τη θαλάσσια οικονομία και τη νησιωτικότητα αντιμέτωπη με τον ανταγωνισμό. Πριν από μερικές μέρες, στο 9ο συνέδριο Υποδομών και Μεταφορών ITC 2026 ο Κωνσταντίνος Γκώνιας, γενικός διευθυντή του Συνδέσμου Επιχειρήσεων Επιβατηγού Ναυτιλίας (ΣΕΕΝ) έκανε λόγο για εκρηκτική άνοδο του λειτουργικού κόστους λόγω των καυσίμων έως και 110%. Η ακτοπλοΐα όπως τόνισε αποτελεί την πιο κρίσιμη υποδομή για την Ελλάδα, καθώς εξασφαλίζει τη σύνδεση των νησιών, τη μεταφορά επιβατών και αγαθών, στηρίζει τον τουρισμό , την κοινωνική και οικονομική συνοχή. «Πίσω από κάθε δρομολόγιο βρίσκεται η επιχείρηση που το οργανώνει, η επένδυση στο πλοίο και το πλήρωμα που αναλαμβάνει την εκτέλεσή του», υπογράμμισε και έθεσε το ζήτημα των σκληρών απαιτήσεων στην καθημερινή λειτουργία ενός επιβατηγού πλοίου, όπου οι προσεγγίσεις στα λιμάνια και η εξυπηρέτηση επιβατών και οχημάτων απαιτούν συγκέντρωση και συνεργασία. Η ανάγκη για έμπειρα πληρώματα, η προσέλκυση και στελέχωση νέων στο επάγγελμα, κρίνεται απαραίτητη για να μπορέσουν οι ακτοπλοϊκές επιχειρήσεις να συνεχίσουν να υπηρετούν τις ανάγκες των νησιών, ιδίως κατά τη θερινή περίοδο τουριστικής αιχμής. Αν και σύμφωνα με στοιχεία του ΝΑΤ, η ετήσια εγγεγραμμένη απασχόληση στα επιβατηγά ακτοπλοϊκά πλοία παρουσιάζει μια μικρή αύξηση 5% (αφού από 5.400 ναυτικούς το 2024 ανήλθαν σε 5.700 το 2025) δεν εξαλείφεται το πρόβλημα. in.title: IT sector likely to report another muted quarter amid global uncertainty
in.description: New Delhi, Oct 4 (IANS) The Indian IT sector is likely to register another muted results (July-September period), in what is typically a seasonally strong quarter, as deal wins remain soft, client decision-making stays cautious, and discretionary spending stays curtailed amid macro uncertainty, according to analysts. Pricing pressure persists as AI-led productivity pass-through gets embedded into renewals and new deals, according to a note by HDFC Securities. “Q2 FY27 (estimated) tier-1 growth is projected at -0.4 per cent to +2.0 per cent QoQ CC and mid-tier companies ranging from +0.6 per cent to +6.3 per cent, partly aided by acquisitions,” said the note. With H1 tracking below expectations, the FY27 recovery rests on H2, which includes the seasonally soft furlough-impacted Q3, tempering full-year expectations. Rupee depreciation, operational efficiencies, and elevated utilisation will offset the wage hikes impact, but AI-led deflation concerns continue to weigh on sector multiples, the note said. Indian IT companies maintain that direct Gen-AI deployment by enterprises remains difficult in complex, regulatory-heavy brownfield environments, keeping the role of system integration (SI) vendors critical. The expected 6-7 per cent deflation impact is being offset by net-new AI-centric deal wins, though conversion remains slow. Growth recovery is a function of execution, as new deals are increasingly outcome-driven, pricing is agent-augmented, and renewals come at a discount, according to the note. Valuations remain near historical lows and FCF yields stay attractive, it added. With Q2 earnings expected to be softer than Q1, market sentiment is likely to remain fragile. Indian equities are likely to stay under pressure in the near term as a record global bond rout, renewed strength in crude and the heaviest foreign selling in six months weigh on sentiment, said analysts. —IANS na/

ae.title: UAE gold prices fall for second straight week, boosting bullion and jewellery demand
ae.description: Dubai: Gold prices extended their decline for a second consecutive week, with prices falling between Dh10.25 and Dh17.5 per gram across different categories compared with the previous week's levels, according to price indicators in Dubai and Sharjah. The latest declines mean gold prices have fallen by a total of Dh28.5 per gram over the past two weeks. The price of 24-carat gold dropped to Dh499 per gram, down Dh17.5 from the end of the previous week. Meanwhile, 22-carat gold fell to Dh462 per gram, a decrease of Dh16.25. The price of 21-carat gold reached Dh443 per gram, down Dh15.5, while 18-carat gold fell to Dh379.75 per gram, a decline of Dh13.25. The price of 14-carat gold stood at Dh296.25 per gram, down Dh10.25. Gold and jewellery retailers said the continued decline in prices has stimulated demand, particularly for bullion and new jewellery purchases. Mohammed Dheeban, Marketing Manager at Al-Rumaizan Gold and Jewellery Trading Company, said the recent decline in gold prices had positively affected market activity. "The significant decline in the price of the yellow metal during the recent period has positively impacted demand in the markets, through a noticeable increase in demand for gold bullion of various types, categories and weights, in addition to the increased demand for buying new gold jewellery gifts," he said. Dheeban added that stronger demand had increased competition among retailers, prompting stores to introduce promotions, incentives and new jewellery designs to attract customers. Ahmed Aneizan, Deputy CEO of Salem Al Shuaibi Jewellery Company, said current price levels were encouraging purchases. "The current gold price levels are encouraging for buying, whether for bullion or new jewellery gifts of various categories, as evidenced by the remarkable activity in the markets recently, with increased demand from customers to buy bullion and jewellery," he said. He added that discounts on making charges and other promotional offers, together with lower gold prices, had contributed to stimulating demand. Manger Balik, Sales Manager at Reg Gold and Jewellery Trading, said the continued decline in prices for a second straight week had attracted investors and traders interested in bullion purchases. "The continued decline in the price of the yellow metal, for the second week in a row and by significant amounts, has contributed to an increase in demand for bullion and attracted traders in this sector, and has also contributed to stimulating demand for gold jewellery gifts," he said.

ae.title: SIBIONICS and PharmaSens Explore New Horizons for Automated Insulin Delivery at EASD 2026
ae.description: MILAN , Oct. 4, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- At the European Association for the Study of Diabetes (EASD) 2026, SiBionics presented "See More, Act Earlier," connecting continuous sensing with future diabetes care. Three exhibition chapters shaped this vision: "See More: Beyond Glucose," covering glucose, ketone and combined monitoring; "Act Earlier: From Insight to Intervention," exploring multimodal sensing and insulin delivery; and "Go Further: Realizing the Unimagined," looking toward broader biosensing applications. The vision was further explored at the SiBionics industry symposium, "From Sensors to Integrated Care: Emerging Technologies Shaping the Future of Diabetes Management." The symposium was chaired by Prof. Mark Evans, of the University of Cambridge and Cambridge University Hospitals, United Kingdom, and Dr. Guido Freckmann, of the Institute for Diabetes-Technology GmbH (IfDT), Germany. Prof. Karolina Kędzierska-Kapuza discussed CGM and individualized care in type 3c diabetes. Prof. Wei Qiang presented CGM accuracy findings and future multimodal sensing concepts. Prof. Andrej Janež explored continuous ketone monitoring in the GLP-1 era. Prof. Ahmad Haidar presented ketone monitoring research and the first findings of the SMART02 feasibility study on integrated glucose sensing and insulin delivery. SMART02 evaluated an early prototype of niia signature, an investigational device jointly developed by PharmaSens and SiBionics since the two companies announced their collaboration in June 2025. niia signature will combine continuous glucose monitoring (CGM), insulin delivery and an automated glucose control (AGC) algorithm in one wearable patch. It aims to reduce the burden of managing separate devices for automated insulin delivery (AID). The study addressed a central integration challenge: maintaining glucose measurement performance when insulin is delivered close to the sensor. Temporary interference after a bolus was uncommon overall and occurred mainly with doses of 10 units or more, where the probability was 20 to 25%. On average, the sensor signal fully recovered approximately 20 minutes after bolus delivery. In the second part of the study, the prototype was also tested together with the AGC algorithm developed by Prof. Ahmad Haidar. The PharmaSens niia patch pump, the SiBionics sensor and the AGC algorithm performed consistently throughout the study. The findings, also featured at the SiBionics booth, mark an early development milestone. Together, the exhibition and symposium connected clinical needs with emerging technologies. Through niia signature, PharmaSens and SiBionics are exploring how integration could make future AID easier to wear and use. Further research is needed to establish its performance and clinical potential. niia signature is an investigational device. It is not approved or cleared in any market and is not available for sale. About SIBIONICS Founded in 2015 and headquartered in Shenzhen, SiBionics is a medical technology company specializing in CGM and multi-parameter health solutions, with nearly 700 professionals worldwide. Combining advanced sensor technology with AI-driven algorithms, the company develops accessible, reliable solutions for chronic disease management. Its multidisciplinary R&D team brings expertise in biosensing, chip design, materials science, and artificial intelligence, supporting innovation from research to commercialization. Through fully in-house CGM systems and continuous monitoring technologies, SiBionics provides real-time data and comprehensive insights to support daily management and better-informed health decisions. Learn more at www.sibionicscgm.com . About PharmaSens PharmaSens AG, a privately owned Swiss company, is dedicated to simplifying diabetes management and broadening the reach of insulin pump therapy. The PharmaSens team has a wealth of experience in diabetes care and medtech device engineering, having contributed to the development of multiple insulin pump generations. Over several years of research and development, PharmaSens has built a patented international portfolio of distinctive and innovative products. For more information, please visit PharmaSens.com . sa.title: دراسة تحذر من تزايد سرطان القولون والمستقيم بين الأطفال والمراهقين
sa.description: حذّرت دراسة أمريكية حديثة من تزايد حالات سرطان القولون والمستقيم بين المراهقين والشباب، بعدما أظهرت أن غالبية المرضى الصغار الذين شملتهم الدراسة لم يُكتشف المرض لديهم إلا في مراحل متقدمة، وسط دعوات للأطباء إلى عدم تجاهل الأعراض المستمرة حتى لدى صغار السن.ووفقاً لنتائج الدراسة التي عُرضت خلال المؤتمر والمعرض الوطني للأكاديمية الأمريكية لطب الأطفال لعام 2026 في سان دييغو، حلّل الباحثون السجلات الطبية لـ84 مريضاً تبلغ أعمارهم 21 عاماً أو أقل، شُخّصوا بسرطان القولون والمستقيم بين عامي 2012 و2023 في عدد من المراكز الطبية. 80% اكتُشف لديهم المرض في مراحل متقدمة وأظهرت النتائج أن 51% من المرضى كانوا في المرحلة الثالثة عند التشخيص، و29% في المرحلة الرابعة، ما يعني أن 80% من الحالات التي شملتها الدراسة كانت قد وصلت إلى مراحل متقدمة.وكان متوسط عمر المرضى عند التشخيص 16.5 عاماً، فيما عانى 74% منهم آلاماً في البطن أو أسفل الظهر، و45% تغيراً في عادات الأمعاء، و43% فقداناً للوزن، و38% نزيفاً من المستقيم. تأخر التشخيص لأسابيع وكشفت الدراسة عن تأخر ملحوظ في الوصول إلى التشخيص؛ إذ استمرت الأعراض لمدة وسطية بلغت 12 أسبوعاً قبل تشخيص المرض، فيما بلغ متوسط الفترة حتى إجراء تنظير القولون 13 أسبوعاً.ويرى الباحثون أن ندرة سرطان القولون والمستقيم لدى صغار السن قد تؤدي إلى إرجاع أعراض مثل آلام البطن وتغير عادات الأمعاء وفقدان الوزن والنزيف إلى أسباب أكثر شيوعاً وأقل خطورة، ما قد يؤخر اكتشاف السرطان. معظم المرضى بلا تاريخ عائلي ومن النتائج اللافتة أن 20% فقط من المرضى كان لديهم قريب من الدرجة الأولى أو الثانية مصاب بسرطان القولون والمستقيم، ما يعني أن معظم الحالات لم يكن لديها تاريخ عائلي معروف للمرض.كما أظهرت تحاليل الأورام انتشار خصائص مرضية عدوانية؛ إذ كانت الأورام ضعيفة التمايز لدى نحو 42% من الحالات، وظهرت الخصائص المخاطية لدى 39%، وخصائص خلايا «الخاتم» لدى 33%. أكثر من ثلث المرضى عانوا عودة السرطان وأظهرت المتابعة أن 36.9% من المرضى تعرضوا لانتكاسة وعودة المرض، بمتوسط بلغ نحو 11 شهراً، وكان نحو 97% ممن عانوا الانتكاسة قد شُخّصوا أصلاً في المرحلتين الثالثة أو الرابعة.وبنهاية فترة الدراسة، توفي 38 مريضاً، أي 45.2% من المجموعة، بسبب سرطان القولون والمستقيم. أعراض لا ينبغي تجاهلها وقالت الباحثة إيريكا أرنولد، زميلة أبحاث جراحة الأطفال والمشاركة في الدراسة، إن سرطان القولون والمستقيم أصبح أكثر شيوعاً لدى المراهقين والشباب، وإنه عند ظهوره في هذه الأعمار غالباً ما يكون عدوانياً ويُكتشف في مراحل متأخرة، مع ارتفاع معدلات الانتكاسة والوفاة.ودعا الباحثون الأطباء إلى وضع سرطان القولون والمستقيم ضمن الاحتمالات التشخيصية عند استمرار أعراض مثل آلام البطن أو أسفل الظهر، والنزيف من المستقيم، وفقدان الوزن غير المبرر، والتغير المستمر في عادات الأمعاء لدى المراهقين، خصوصاً عندما لا يوجد تفسير آخر واضح لهذه الأعراض.وأكّدت الدراسة أهمية زيادة الوعي بالمرض لدى الفئات العمرية الصغيرة وتسريع التشخيص عند ظهور علامات تستدعي الفحص، في ظل المؤشرات المتزايدة على إصابة أشخاص أصغر سناً بسرطان القولون والمستقيم.

za.title: Citi explains why home improvement stocks are lagging in 2026
How Medicare deal survived Masemola’s order to stop it
za.description: Suspended national police commissioner Gen Fannie Masemola wanted the R360-million Medicare24 health contract stopped after being warned of possible corruption, yet the deal survived and was awarded weeks later, despite repeated pleas for an investigation. A tranche of affidavits that Sunday World has seen reveals that Masemola initially took the warning seriously enough to recommend stopping the award. But after being told everything appeared proper “on paper”, the process continued. The trail began with suspended senior Idac investigator Suneel Bellochun, who approached Maj-Gen Fred Kekana about the tender. On May 8, 2024, Bellochun sent Kekana company records, procurement documents and information concerning Medicare24 Tshwane District, linked to businessman Vusimuzi “Cat” Matlala. Bellochun wanted an investigation into the affairs of Medicare24 before the Bid Adjudication Committee approved the award. “I forwarded the messages to national commissioner Gen Masemola for his intervention,” Kekana states. Thirteen days later, Masemola called Maj-Gen Senobea Julie Hankins. Hankins says Masemola told her he had received information that the contract was about to be awarded to a person allegedly linked to the murder of Tembisa Hospital whistleblower Babita Deokaran. Hankins says Masemola instructed her to establish the status of the award quietly, “without raising the alarm”. When Hankins returned to her office, she discovered that the submission was already before the committee that day. She approached Bid Evaluation Committee chair Brig AT Ngema, who told her the evaluation had followed the prescribed process and he had found no obvious evidence of criminal activity. Hankins sent Masemola the feedback on May 21, but “did not receive any response from the national commissioner,” she states, and they never discussed it again. Another affidavit raises questions about the due diligence behind the assurances. Cpt Ramasela Flora Matjeke, who attended Medicare24’s April assessment, says, “There was no physical inspection done… Everything was just a presentation prepared by Medicare 24.” The contract nevertheless went ahead. Maj-Gen Liesbeth Matobako says SAPS ultimately paid Medicare24 R48.65-million during 2024/25 – later declared irregular expenditure, and another R1.66-million thereafter. Another R862,128.72 invoice was frozen after the contract was terminated. Hankins says she had expected Masemola to intervene and prevent the award “by any means necessary”.

za.title: BMF president grilled over R1.2m in irregular payments
za.description: Black Management Forum (BMF) president Mpho Motsei has been asked to account for more than R1.2 million in payments made to him or on his behalf over nearly two years, including stakeholder engagement payments, accommodation, travel and other expenses. In a letter dated September 30, BMF Young Professionals chairperson and director Jeremiah Klaas requested supporting documents and explanations for payments totalling R1 228 352.15 recorded between November 2024 and September this year. Klaas said the payments appeared in the BMF’s transaction history and that the board needed to understand the purpose, authority and supporting documentation for the expenditure. He said he had reached no conclusions and was seeking clarity so the board could account for the transactions to members and auditors. Klaas said R599 088 31 was paid into Motsei’s bank account through 48 transactions. A further R475 582.27 was spent on hotels; R115 787.94 on flights; R14 006.84 on Uber, car hire and fuel; and R25 000 on a seat at the Progressive Business Forum Presidential Dinner. A major concern was 33 payments totalling R486 952.78 that were recorded as “stakeholder engagement”. Klaas said the payments, made from March last year, at roughly two-week intervals, ranged from R7 332 to R28 774. The records did not identify the claims, events or documentation supporting the payments. He questioned whether they amounted to a recurring allowance and, if so, who authorised it. Klaas also highlighted six payments totalling R83 684.73 made between June and August this year, despite no flights, hotels or transport allegedly being booked for Motsei after May 22. The letter further questioned possible duplication of travel costs. Klaas said Motsei received seven Cape Town travel claims worth R53 120.23 between January and March last year, while the BMF paid for flights and accommodation linked to trips during the same period. Klaas identified 23 hotel stays in Sandton and Johannesburg costing R196 050.33 and five stays in Limpopo totalling R22 172. Two bookings were described as “staycations”. He asked where Motsei was living at the time, who approved the bookings and why some expenses were paid to him rather than to service providers. Klaas also queried two payments of R13 932.90 made on the same day in September last year and asked whether one should be repaid. The BMF memorandum of incorporation limits payments to directors to legitimate reimbursements, payments under bona fide agreements and obligations arising from legal commitments. Klaas noted that elected directors were not entitled to remuneration except where provisions applied to full-time executive leadership. He requested policies, resolutions and approvals authorising the payments, together with invoices, receipts, travel records and details of engagements funded by the organisation. He also asked whether any of the expenses were claimed from other organisations or whether Motsei received additional benefits linked to the forum. Motsei was given until Wednesday to respond. Klaas warned that if the explanation was inadequate, he would place the matter before the board and consider referring it to the auditors. Motsei had not responded by the time of publication. The dispute comes amid a governance battle in the BMF. In July, Sunday World revealed that a report by BMF stalwarts recommended action against Motsei and directors of the organisation’s investment arm over governance and financial concerns. Motsei has rejected the findings and counter-suspended individuals he claims are attempting to hijack the organisation. The report, chaired by former BMF leader and MK Party MP Mzwanele Manyi, found that investment arm directors allegedly awarded themselves increases without shareholder approval and declared a R31m dividend in July 2024 without conducting a solvency and liquidity test.

za.title: R730bn in eight hands, yet millions languish in poverty
za.description: South Africa’s eight billionaires, all of them men, have a combined fortune of R730-billion, while more than 23-million people live below the national poverty line, a new Oxfam South Africa report has found. The report, Hoarded Wealth, Dignity Denied, describes a country where the gap between the haves and the have-nots has grown wider over three decades of democracy, not narrower. According to Oxfam, the country’s richest billionaire alone owns more than twice the combined wealth of the poorest 70% of the population. On average, someone in the bottom 90% would need 345 years to build the wealth held by the typical person in the richest 1%. The fortunes are growing fast. Last year the country’s then-seven billionaires added the equivalent of R382m to their wealth every day. Their combined real wealth has grown by 130% since 2020. In 1994 the richest 1% held just under half of the national wealth. By 2024 that share had climbed to 54.9%. Over the same period, the bottom half of the population slid deeper into the red. Their debts now outweigh everything they own. Since 2019 the richest 1% have captured 56% of all new wealth created in the country. The bottom 90% got just 14%. The divide remains starkly racial. Black households own, on average, just 5% of the wealth of white households. Black South Africans make up 82% of the population but 93.6% of those live below the poverty line. Almost two-thirds of households are food insecure. Official unemployment has climbed from 25% in 2015 to 33.6% in the second quarter of this year, against a G20 average of about 6%. The report notes that one of the country’s highest-paid CEOs earns in less than four hours what a domestic worker on the minimum wage earns in a whole year. Even the wealthy are uneasy. A 2025 survey of South African dollar millionaires found that 65% believe extreme wealth threatens democracy and 64% support higher taxes on the very rich. Oxfam says a moderate net wealth tax alone could raise an extra $9.15bn (roughly R150bn) a year. It wants government to introduce a wealth tax, raise taxes on dividends and close tax breaks that mostly benefit high earners. Among its five key demands is a National Inequality Reduction Plan with time-bound targets to cut the income Gini coefficient to 0.3. By most estimates, South Africa’s Gini is the highest in the world. The plan also calls for a universal basic income, more investment in health, education and care work and putting women at the centre of economic policy. The report is critical of the grant system. The Social Relief of Distress grant reaches only about 8.5-million people and is worth less than half the food poverty line. Oxfam insists inequality is not inevitable. It is, the report argues, “the result of policy choices” and it can be reversed with political will.

za.title: Youth are ditching medical aid as affordability crisis deepens
za.description: The rising cost of private healthcare has come under renewed scrutiny after it emerged that a growing number of young South Africans are opting not to join medical schemes when they enter the workforce. Paresh Prema, the branch head of health actuarial services at Alexforbes, said the trend was placing pressure on medical schemes, which had traditionally relied on younger, healthier members to subsidise older members who make greater use of healthcare services. For decades, medical schemes have operated on a risk-pooling model in which younger members, who generally have fewer chronic health conditions and lower healthcare use, help offset the costs of older members. Prema said the dynamic was changing, contributing to escalating healthcare costs and above-inflation contribution increases. Prema, who was speaking at the Hospital Association of SA’s Quality and Conference 2026 held in Sandton last week, noted that medical scheme coverage has stagnated and even declined slightly over the past decade. In 2012, 15.9% of South Africans had access to medical aid, compared with 15.5% in 2024. As a result, Prema said, legislative reform might be necessary to increase participation in medical schemes, including measures that would compel employed individuals to obtain medical cover while introducing covers that would be affordable for low-income earners. His comments come after the Board of Healthcare Funders earlier this year failed in its court bid to compel the Council for Medical Schemes (CMS) to allow the introduction of low-cost benefit options, which are more affordable products that do not provide the full range of prescribed minimum benefits. Prema said: “In terms of demographics, we have seen that the period from 2012 to 2024 the increase in average age has been gradual but the older members increase the chronic prevalence, service intensity. “All of these have an effect in driving contribution increases. The effect is compounding overtime. That is quite an important aspect that we still monitor and that drives costs and we need to ensure what solutions we put in place to deal with that.” Prema also highlighted the persistent trend of medical aid contribution increases outpacing consumer inflation. According to reports, Discovery Health Medical Scheme has announced an average contribution increase of 8.2% for next year and Momentum Health 7.9%, both well above the CMS’s recommended 3.8%. The increases are also far above and consumer inflation, currently running at 4.4%. “We find that members are buying options that are cheaper … that is also due to rising costs and higher entry price. “That results in declining participation and a narrow cross subsidy between the younger and older members, as well ageing pool. “This cycle continues without there being any solution in between to try to deal with the affordability crisis. “We see that the increase in membership is not in line with the increase in the population but an increase with the GDP. The more people get formal employment, the more they get to afford medical scheme cover,” he said. Prema said it was becoming increasingly evident that private healthcare services were becoming less affordable and warned that, without intervention, the situation was unlikely to improve. Breaking down medical scheme expenditure, he said hospitals accounted for 35.95% of costs, specialists 28.02%, medicines 14.05% and allied health services 8.47%. “Affordability of one member’s response affects all the remaining members. That’s why retention is important in this space …and participation is very core to managing costs,” he said. University of Cape Town Professor Susan Cleary said South Africa’s healthcare spending patterns highlighted the stark differences between the public and private sectors. The private healthcare sector spent about R249-billion annually to serve the 15% of South Africans covered by medical schemes. By comparison, the public healthcare system, which serves 85% of the population, receives about R243-billion in tax-payer funding. Combined healthcare expenditure amounts to roughly R492-billion a year. This translates into annual healthcare spending of about R23 000 per medical scheme beneficiary, compared with about R5 000 per person in the public healthcare system. Cleary questioned whether universal private-sector healthcare coverage would be financially sustainable. She said that if every South African were covered by a medical scheme, annual expenditure would rise to about R1.4-trillion, about 30% of GDP. By comparison, universal coverage through the public sector would cost an estimated R299bn, or about 5.8% of GDP. While a universal public healthcare system would require increased government spending and potentially higher taxes, Cleary said it would remain significantly more affordable than extending private medical scheme cover to the entire population. “Then you have to ask: Does it make sense to spend 30% of GDP on healthcare?” Cleary added that the level of expenditure would be exceptional by international standards.

za.title: Leaders South Africa has yet to learn to celebrate
za.description: When a black professional reaches the top of a strategic institution in South Africa, their arrival is rarely presented as news about one person. Transformation remains highly contested even after 32 years of democracy. That is why the reappointment of Mteto Nyati as chairperson of Eskom for a further three years matters well beyond Megawatt Park. The Black Business Council welcomes it for reasons that are symbolic and strategic. Media personality Redi Tlhabi’s recent column in Daily Maverick asked why South Africa finds it so difficult to credit black leadership with success. The Black Business Council would add a second question: What does it cost the country when that credit is withheld? Not long ago, families cooked by candlelight and planned their lives around load-shedding schedules. Many respected analysts warned that the grid would not stabilise for years. That forecast has not come to pass. Load-shedding has effectively ended, the grid has stabilised and Eskom has returned to profitability. Thousands of Eskom employees did the work on the ground. Under Dr Nyati as chair and Dan Marokane as chief executive, the work was given direction, discipline and protection from distraction. Few state-owned enterprises have moved from sustained crisis to stability so quickly. Eskom’s recovery remains unfinished, and difficult decisions on transmission investment, municipal debt and market reform lie ahead. But the country faces those decisions from a position of strength rather than emergency. That shift did not happen by itself. Nor is this Nyati’s first success. Over a career spanning nearly four decades, he has built a record that would be celebrated in most economies. Trained as a mechanical engineer at the then University of Natal, he began his career at Afrox, spent more than a decade at IBM and later led Microsoft South Africa as managing director. At MTN he helped return a struggling business to growth. At Altron he steered a group, founded during apartheid, into a new era. It is not by accident that Nyati titled his memoir Betting on a Darkie. The title is uncomfortable by design. It names the wager South African institutions have long hesitated to make and the burden carried by those on whom the bet is placed. Early in his career, he was often the only black engineer in the room, advised above all not to fail. Nearly four decades later, he is still asked to prove what his record shows. A pattern of that kind is not an accident. It is a method. Business schools, which rightly teach the turnarounds of global corporations, would do well to study Dr Nyati as a case in what transformed leadership looks like: engineering depth, commercial discipline and a steady hand in institutions under strain. Yet South Africa has a curious way of assigning authority. André de Ruyter led Eskom through the most severe load-shedding the country has experienced. He continues to be sought out as a leading voice on the utility’s future, while leaders associated with its recovery are often asked to justify their place. Why do De Ruyter’s words seem to carry an authority his results did not earn? Nyati has not been beyond criticism, nor should he be. His caution on the pace and sequencing of unbundling has drawn sharp responses from parts of organised business and the energy commentariat. The council supports reform of the electricity sector. We also recognise that a chair who asks how restructuring will affect Eskom’s debt and obligations to lenders is exercising fiduciary duty, not resisting change. A prominent energy commentator who called for his departure in August has since praised his leadership as quiet, authoritative and principled. The shift is welcome. It also shows how quickly caution from a black leader can be read as obstruction. The strategic case extends beyond Eskom. Energy, transport, water, ports and digital infrastructure will shape the country’s growth for a generation. Black engineers, financiers and executives are building careers in these sectors. What they watch closely is how the country treats those who reach the top. For the Black Business Council, transformation in strategic sectors is not a favour extended to black professionals, but a test of whether the country uses the full depth of its talent where the stakes are highest. After years in which Eskom’s leadership came and went with alarming speed, continuity at board level also offers what the utility has lacked most: stability long enough to finish the job. South Africa’s history has left a lingering assumption that black leaders hold their positions on sufferance. Nyati’s reappointment offers a chance to retire that assumption. The council will continue to stand with black professionals who build and lead the institutions this country depends on. We will also keep asking a question that reaches beyond one boardroom: How many Mteto Nyatis are out there, fighting for their survival, when they should be celebrated? Matabane is the chief executive of the Black Business Council.

za.title: R30 petrol: The shock our country cannot afford
za.description: There is a number that should make every South African sit up and take notice: R30 a litre. That is where 95 unleaded petrol is expected to go next week when the latest fuel-price adjustment takes effect, with diesel expected to rise above R33 a litre. According to the Central Energy Fund’s latest calculation, inland 95 petrol could increase by about R3.21 a litre, from R26.92 to roughly R30.13. Diesel is facing increases of around R3 a litre. While the final adjustment is to be announced, the new prices are expected to take effect on October 7. This is about far more than the cost of filling a tank. Fuel is an input into almost every part of the economy. It moves people and goods and affects farming, manufacturing, construction, logistics and virtually every business that depends on transport. When diesel prices rise sharply, those costs filter through to the prices consumers pay for goods and services. Economists refer to this as cost-push inflation. South Africa is being hit by this shock at a difficult moment. The fuel increase is being driven largely by higher international oil prices and a weaker rand. Brent crude ended September at around $100 (R1 700) a barrel, while the rand weakened against the dollar. Exchange rates are influenced by global interest rates, bond yields, investor sentiment, commodity prices and domestic economic conditions. The US Federal Reserve raised rates by 25 basis points in September to 3.75%-4%, while the South African Reserve Bank increased its repo rate by 25 basis points to 7.25%. Higher global interest rates can encourage investors to shift capital towards developed markets. At the same time, a weaker rand raises the cost of imported fuel and other goods. The result is a triple squeeze: higher fuel prices, a weaker currency and higher interest rates, affecting an economy struggling to generate meaningful growth. South Africa’s inflation rate stood at 4.4% in August but the Reserve Bank has warned that inflation will probably move above 5% later this year and into early next year. The danger is the increase in the petrol price spreads through the economy. Transport costs rise. Businesses face higher operating expenses. Producers increase prices. Consumers have less disposable income. Spending elsewhere declines. Companies become more cautious about investment and hiring. The multiplier effect begins working in reverse. The economic growth forecast remains 1.2% for the year. However, the economy contracted by 0.2% in the second quarter after growing by 0.4% in the first quarter. Manufacturing declined by 1.8%, while mining shrank by 3%. The Reserve Bank expects a recovery during the second half of the year but it has also acknowledged that risks to growth are tilted to the downside. What happens if that recovery does not materialise? Negative real growth cannot simply be dismissed. It has become a risk that deserves serious consideration. The consequences would be significant. South Africa is not entering a potential slowdown from a position of strength. Unemployment remains high. Investment is weak. Businesses are under pressure and households are grappling with rising living costs. That is why economic growth is the mechanism through which jobs are created, incomes expand, investment is attracted and households gain financial breathing room. Without growth, the cycle turns negative. Higher fuel costs reduce disposable income. Rising production expenses squeeze business margins. Inflation puts pressure on interest rates. Higher borrowing costs suppress spending and investment. Softer demand then discourages companies from expanding or hiring. That is the negative multiplier effect. It is something South Africa can ill afford. The country cannot control global oil prices, geopolitical tension in the Middle East, US monetary policy or international capital flows. What it can influence is whether the domestic economy is resilient enough to absorb those external shocks. The question is whether South Africa can continue absorbing one shock after another without undermining the growth it so desperately needs. For a country facing deep unemployment, inequality and economic challenges, the question is one that should concern every South African. Maarten van Doesburgh is an economist, head of economics at CPUT, CEO of Economics Investment Group and a regular commentator on South Africa’s economic landscape.

za.title: The slimming squeeze
za.description: For South Africans looking for an alternative way to lose weight, the latest pitch is to get the treatment now and pay for it over time. A new doctor-led service is trying to make popular GLP-1 medicines easier to access through virtual consultations and payment options. The appeal is easy to understand. Registered GLP-1 medicines typically cost between R3 000 and R6 000 a month, before consultation fees. For many people using them for weight management rather than diabetes, the price puts treatment out of reach. Obiflex, the doctor-led health service, is selling itself on affordability and says pricing created a market for cheaper compounded versions. “Now the compounding route has been shut down by the South African Health Products Regulatory Authority (Sahpra) and South African Pharmacy Council (SAPC). So, unless there’s legitimate, affordable access, that demand doesn’t disappear; it risks people seeking other unregulated or illicit options,” co-founder and CEO Shaun Barns says. Compounded medicines are prepared for an individual patient when a suitable commercial product is not available. In practice, however, regulators say some sellers went much further, producing and marketing GLP-1 products for wider distribution. Sahpra and the SAPC have cracked down on pharmacies they say were illegally compounding weight-loss medicines, including semaglutide and tirzepatide. Their investigation focused on products made at a Pretoria pharmacy under the iDexis brand. The regulators flagged questions about how active pharmaceutical ingredients were imported, whether products were properly tested for identity, potency and purity and whether the equipment and conditions were suitable for sterile preparation. They also warned doctors and pharmacists that prescribing or dispensing the flagged medicines could lead to disciplinary action. “While compounding is strictly limited to the preparation of medicines for individual patients based on a valid prescription, the facility was found to be manufacturing and marketing GIP/GLP-1-based products, including semaglutide, tirzepatide, and combination formulations, for broader commercial distribution,” the watchdogs said after their operation in June. Danish pharmaceutical company Novo Nordisk is the patent owner and original developer of semaglutide and brands such as Ozempic, Wegovy and Rybelsus. Since its patent has been reproduced on the black market for far less, undercutting its profits, it has launched an awareness campaign, warning that its testing shows that compounding semaglutide often involves synthetic processes that can compromise safety. According to Obiflex, however, the regulatory crackdown in South Africa has exposed a broader challenge: What happens to patients who cannot afford the regulated products? The company estimates that as many as 300 000 South Africans have been affected and puts the local appetite for weight-loss GLP-1 medicines at about R3-billion. Its alternative is a virtual consultation with a doctor who can prescribe a registered medicine, with the cost structured to make treatment easier to manage. Barns says many patients turned to unregistered compounded products because they were cheaper. Closing that route without creating an affordable alternative, he argues, will not make the demand disappear. Barns says the company’s doctors have received specialist training in endocrinology and cardiology of weight management from co-founder Dr Riaz Motara. The aim, he says, is to look at the factors behind unhealthy weight changes rather than focusing only on the number on the scale. The appeal of a slimmer silhouette sometimes leads patients to the black market, with the hope of getting drugs quicker and cheaper. Although there has been a shift and progress to be accepting of all body types, being thin remains a sought-after goal.

ml.title: Birahim Soumaré : « Notre diplomatie repose sur la défense des intérêts nationaux »
ml.description: © Internet Ancien ambassadeur du Mali en Türkiye et analyste en stratégie internationale, Birahim Soumaré expose les principes d’une diplomatie attachée à sa liberté de décision. Il évoque la diversification des partenariats, la médiation et le suivi des engagements conclus avec les États. Sur quels principes la diplomatie malienne doit-elle s’appuyer ? La démarche diplomatique définie par le Chef de l’État repose sur la défense des intérêts nationaux et la diversification des partenaires. Elle doit permettre au Mali de travailler avec différents États sans renoncer à ses priorités. Nos relations s’inscrivent dans le respect mutuel, la souveraineté, la non-ingérence et la recherche d’intérêts communs. La diplomatie sert d’abord à créer les conditions permettant au pays de défendre sa sécurité, son développement et sa place dans les relations internationales. Cette coopération doit rester ouverte et non exclusive. La diversification des partenariats peut-elle entraîner le Mali dans les rivalités entre puissances ? La nature de notre relation avec un pays ne saurait être déterminée par les relations que nous entretenons avec un autre. Notre dynamique diplomatique doit s’orienter en fonction de nos intérêts, et non des incompréhensions ou des rivalités géostratégiques opposant des nations. Nous avons l’expérience d’une politique équidistante envers les partenaires avec lesquels nous travaillons. Cette approche permet de conserver la liberté de définir chaque relation selon ce qu’elle apporte au Mali. Le Mali possède-t-il une tradition diplomatique susceptible de soutenir cette liberté ? Notre pays dispose d’une histoire diplomatique importante. Il a notamment contribué au règlement de la Guerre des Sables entre l’Algérie et le Maroc. La signature à Bamako, le 2 novembre 1963, de l’accord de cessez-le-feu entre les deux pays a consacré la contribution de la diplomatie et de l’armée maliennes à la recherche d’une solution pacifique. Cette expérience montre que le Mali peut entretenir de bonnes relations avec plusieurs partenaires, préserver son équilibre et contribuer au règlement des différends. Comment faire pour que les engagements diplomatiques produisent des résultats concrets ? Les Commissions mixtes constituent des outils diplomatiques. Elles permettent de reprendre les accords antérieurs, d’examiner leur mise en œuvre et d’intégrer les demandes exprimées par les différents départements ministériels dans l’énergie, l’éducation, la formation ou le commerce. Mais la volonté politique doit être traduite en engagements concrets, suivis et évaluables. Il faut une feuille de route claire, un mécanisme de suivi des accords et des priorités précises. Sans cette continuité, les rencontres produisent des textes sans donner toute leur portée à la coopération.

zw.title: Matters of Health Pinktober- A time to prioritise breast cancer
zw.description: WE are in a new month and it is important to note that October is the month of raising awareness around breast cancer. The month-long movement, known as Pinktober has attracted the attention of women and men across Zimbabwe and the world as they highlight the work around awareness, screening, treatment and care of breast cancer. Furthermore, pink is the selected colour that symbolises work around breast cancer with a pink ribbon pinned on one’s breast area showing that they are breast cancer aware. In Zimbabwe cancer services are offered at all levels of the healthcare system with care concentrated at tertiary and quaternary levels. Several gaps however exist in access, availability, affordability and quality of services that need to be addressed. Prevention offers the most cost-effective strategy for control of cancer. Integration of screening and early detection in other existing health programs will give optimal public health benefits with minimal cost implication and long-term cancer control benefits. However, in Zimbabwe, breast cancer is the second most common cancer in women after cervical cancer (ZNCR, 2022). Data from the cancer registry report also shows a consistent increase in the number of cases diagnosed. Prevention is the most cost-effective intervention. Thirty to forty percent of cancers are preventable by avoiding known risk factors. The main factors contributing to the increasing incidence of cancer in Zimbabwe include: ·Tobacco use ·Alcohol use ·Unhealthy diets ·Physical inactivity ·Environmental factors Key strategies to reduce incidence of cancer include ·Community education and awareness campaigns ·Integration of cancer prevention into school curricula or occupational health programs ·Promotion of healthy diets through local food initiatives ·Physical activity programs ·Stronger tobacco control policies ·Alcohol use reduction initiatives ·Vaccination drives for Human Papilloma Virus ·Regular screening programs for high-risk populations Environmental health initiatives can help to improve living conditions such as safer mining practices, while collaboration with traditional and faith-based healers will enhance community engagement in cancer awareness. The Ministry of Health and Child Care notes that advocacy for supportive strategic policies and investment in research will ensure a comprehensive framework for cancer prevention, ultimately reducing the burden of cancer and improving public health outcomes in Zimbabwe. Cancer treatment is very expensive when people come late to the hospital. Medical experts note that the whole purpose of screening is to catch the disease before it is too late, cancer requires early diagnosis and early treatment then one can minimise the costs of treatment. When one comes late usually that patient will be very sick and they require extensive surgery, hospital stay and recovery which is costly so the whole purpose of early screening is to detect the disease early and save money in treatment. You are what you eat. Many of the healthy eating habits that may reduce the risk of breast cancer recurrence and improve survival also help overall health. The most important lifestyle recommendation after a breast cancer diagnosis is to achieve and maintain a healthy body weight by making gradual changes to the way you eat and by becoming more physically active. Health experts recommend that people ‘create a rainbow in their plate’ by eating plenty of different coloured vegetables and fruit every day. The deeper the colour, the more antioxidants and phytonutrients (like flavonoids, phenolics, lutein, carotenoids) the fruit or vegetable contains. Eat foods like red cabbage, beetroot, dark green leaves like spinach, rape and kovo, carrots, butternut and pumpkin, mangoes, red/purple plums, kiwi fruit, orange peaches, green melon, pomegranates, oranges, nec-tarines, berries. Make fresh juices from these fruits and vegetables too. Antioxidants protect your cells from free radicals that can and damage cells cause cancer. While eating health is recommended, it is essential to choose sensible portion sizes. You might already be eating the right foods, but it could be that you are eating too much. Occasionally measure the amount of food you serve yourself and pay special attention to higher calorie foods such as high fat meats, fried foods, desserts and added fats. Remember to wear pink, to raise awareness this October. #Pinktober #BreastCancer —@NyembeziMu

zw.title: 6 000 screened for breast cancer at UBH … as 66 test positive
zw.description: Robin Muchetu, Health and Gender Editor MORE than 6 000 women attended the United Bulawayo Hospitals (UBH) Visual Inspection with Acetic Acid (VIAC) clinic in 2025 for cervical cancer screening with 5 500 agreeing to breast screening where three hundred women had breast problems requiring attention while 66 were diagnosed with breast cancer. This has been made possible by the free combined cervical and breast cancer screening services offered at UBH where women are offered multiple services during a single visit to the hospital. Dr Munyaradzi Magara, who runs the VIAC clinic at UBH, said the model was working well because women did not have to visit the hospital on different days for different services. “Last year, 6 000 women came through the VIAC clinic. Of those, about 5 500 agreed to have a breast examination. About 300 were found to have some kind of problem and were referred to a clinic. Following further evaluations, 66 new breast cancers were diagnosed last year through this combined cervical and breast screening model. Patients are also still being diagnosed through the general outpatients department, that has not stopped,” said Dr Magara. While some patients are diagnosed through the outpatients department, Dr Magara said they usually had advanced disease. The hospital wants women to seek help earlier, before the disease spreads. “Some patients with breast cancer come through the outpatients department, but we have modified that model because most of those patients are at an advanced stage. More than 60 per cent come to us with advanced breast cancer, when we cannot do much to cure them. “We manage their symptoms and can provide chemotherapy, but treatment is more palliative. In most cases, we are really just managing the symptoms of patients who come through the general outpatients department,” he said. Women and men who notice any changes in their breasts have been encouraged to report to hospital as soon as possible. Dr Magara said a recent masterclass at the institution, led by UK-based surgeons from the Association of Breast Surgery (ABS), provided an opportunity to train more breast specialists. “It was about updating them and keeping them abreast of new techniques in breast surgery. This year, a new level of complexity has been added to the masterclass - reconstructive surgery. “Importantly, we also received a donation of audio-visual equipment from the UK. It is now on site and we have been using it. This has enabled us to reach a larger audience of surgeons,” said Dr Magara. The 20 surgeons taking part in the training were able to watch some procedures in real time from another location. “While the operation was taking place in theatre, we were observing it here at the School of Nursing. The theatre is 400 to 500 metres away. We could hear the commentary and ask questions because we now have this equipment. That is important for expanding our training capabilities. “Under normal circumstances, you cannot have 10 surgeons around the operating table. During this masterclass, only a few were in theatre, as is usual. You cannot enter the sterile field and so on. However, 20 people were able to watch the operation, follow it in real time and ask questions, thanks to the donated equipment,” said Dr Magara. Dr Dick Rainsbury, a specialist surgeon from the UK’s ABS, was training local specialists as part of the masterclass at UBH. He performed specialised breast surgery on a local woman with cancer, removing her breast. “It just takes a while to do. The problem is that breast implants are not used in this country because they are too expensive for breast reconstruction. It is much quicker if you can insert an implant and create a breast straight away. Instead, you have to use tissue from another part of the body. Common sites from which to take tissue are the abdominal wall and the back although tissue from the thighs can also be used. “Although the operation may take three or four hours, the breast is removed and replaced with tissue from the back. Once it has healed, it lasts forever. It is your own tissue, it moves with you and ages with you,” said Dr Rainsbury. “It also tolerates radiotherapy if that treatment is needed. It is a more complicated procedure, but it is an investment worth making. mg.title: ÉDUCATION - Des écoles se retrouvent dans l’embarras du choix
mg.description: La Plateforme des directions nationales de l’enseignement privé (PDNE) et le ministère de l’Enseignement supérieur et de la Recherche scientifique se sont entendus sur l’examen du baccalauréat. Andovola Rabetsimba, directrice du lycée privé Diadema à Ampatsakana. L’annonce d’options A, C et D au sein des catégories L et S pour le baccalauréat 2027, faite par le ministère de l’Enseignement supérieur et de la Recherche scientifique lors d’une réunion avec les acteurs de l’éducation du privé, le 1er octobre, change la donne pour les établissements scolaires privés. Après la publication du décret supprimant ces anciennes séries, au début de cette année scolaire, certaines écoles privées avaient déjà appliqué le nouveau programme et ont remplacé les séries A, C et D par les séries Littéraire, Scientifique et Organisation-Société-Économie. « Nous ne savons pas quel programme appliquer, après cette nouvelle décision. L’ancien et le nouveau programme sont différents. Le nouveau est bon, mais nous avons des difficultés avec les documents », indique Andovola Rabetsimba, directrice du lycée privé Diadema à Ampatsakana, hier. Un autre lycée privé qui a déjà choisi cette voie, pareillement, est certain que parmi ses candidats au baccalauréat, certains vont opter pour les anciennes séries. « Les élèves jugent l’ancien programme plus simple, avec des coefficients plus abordables dans les matières de base. Pour eux, le choix est donc évident. La situation est plus compliquée pour nous, qui avons déjà commencé le nouveau programme et les nouvelles séries », lance un responsable pédagogique d’une école privée. Réflexion Dans les lycées publics, dont la plupart appliquent les nouvelles séries depuis quelques années, cette nouvelle décision ne change pas grand-chose. « En tant qu’établissement public, nous maintenons, certainement, ce qui a été décidé en début d’année. Le programme enseigné, cette année, correspond d’ailleurs à cette décision », lance un enseignant. Les écoles confessionnelles catholiques n’ont pas non plus cette difficulté. « Cette décision nous arrange encore plus, car nous avons commencé l’année scolaire avec l’ancien programme et les anciennes séries », indique le père Jules Ranaivosoa, secrétaire général de la Commission épiscopale pour l’éducation et l’enseignement catholique. Les écoles qui ont déjà fait le pas vers le nouveau programme prennent le temps de la réflexion. La décision se prendra en réunion avec les parents d’élèves. « Nous attendons que l’État publie l’analyse des épreuves pour trancher. Le choix des candidats en dépend», explique Andovola Rabetsimba. Le ministère de l’Enseignement supérieur et de la Recherche scientifique souligne que la nouvelle décision n’est pas un retour en arrière. « Les anciennes séries (A, C, D) ne reviennent pas complètement sous leur ancienne forme, mais il s’agit d’une période de transition pour faciliter le passage au nouveau programme», indique un responsable auprès du ministère. Ainsi, le nouveau système est maintenu. « Les trois grandes catégories de la réforme, dont L pour Littéraire, S pour Scientifique et OSE pour Organisation-Société-Économie, restent la base officielle du nouveau programme d’enseignement », poursuit notre source. Ce ministère et les écoles privées se seraient mis d’accord pour intégrer des sous-options familières au sein de ces nouvelles catégories, pour le baccalauréat 2027. Dans la catégorie L, les candidats ont la possibilité de choisir entre l’option L, A1 ou A2. Dans la catégorie S, ils peuvent choisir entre l’option S, C ou D. « Ce qui permet de retrouver les profils traditionnels axés sur les mathématiques poussées ou les sciences de la vie et de la Terre», précise notre source. Le ministère de l’Enseignement supérieur confirme qu’il s’agit d’une transition pour les élèves de terminale qui étaient en première A, C ou D l’an dernier, ainsi que pour les redoublants de ces séries. Les écoles catholiques et d’autres écoles privées maintiennent pour leur part leur position. « Le nouveau programme d’enseignement comporte encore de nombreuses zones d’ombre», insiste le père Jules Ranaivosoa. Miangaly Ralitera

mg.title: ANNIVERSAIRE DE LA 1RE RÉPUBLIQUE - L’État clarifie le statut du 14 octobre
mg.description: Le 14 octobre devrait être déclaré chômé mais payé. Entreprises, écoles et administrations attendent encore la confirmation officielle de l’État. La date du 14 octobre coïncide aussi avec celle de la prise de pouvoir des militaires en 2025. Le statut du mercredi 14 octobre n’est pas encore officiellement fixé. Selon les premières informations communiquées aux responsables de la communication du ministère de la Fonction publique, du Travail et des Lois sociales, cette journée devrait être déclarée chômée mais payée. La décision doit toutefois encore être officialisée par le texte attendu à l’issue du Conseil des ministres. Cette clarification est particulièrement attendue par les entreprises et les travailleurs, qui doivent déterminer les modalités d’organisation de leurs activités. À SITA SARL, le principe annoncé est de se conformer aux dispositions qui seront finalement arrêtées par les autorités. Les établissements scolaires privés sont également concernés par cette décision. À l’école privée Voltaire, le professeur Rojo Vilolette appelle à davantage de clarté dans les décisions de l’État. La publication du texte officiel doit notamment permettre aux établissements de définir l’organisation des cours et du personnel. Modalités applicables Le statut de cette journée aura également des incidences sur les administrations, les banques, les commerces et les transports. Les dispositions arrêtées par l’État détermineront ainsi le fonctionnement de ces différents secteurs le 14 octobre. Selon une source au sein du ministère de la Fonction publique, du Travail et des Lois sociales, la décision doit encore être officialisée à l’issue du Conseil des ministres. Une communication devrait ensuite préciser les modalités applicables. En parallèle, les préparatifs des festivités du 14 octobre se poursuivent. mg.title: INCLUSION FINANCIÈRE - La digitalisation et les services financiers à démocratiser
mg.description: L’essor du mobile money a transformé l’écosystème financier du pays. Si l’accès aux services financiers mobiles s’est facilité, leur utilisation reste à élargir, notamment pour les paiements du quotidien. Alexandre Castel, CEO de Mvola. Le mobile money est devenu incontournable dans le paysage financier malgache. Plusieurs entreprises accélèrent leurs efforts pour attirer davantage d’utilisateurs et élargir l’accès aux services financiers numériques. Hier, lors d’une rencontre avec la presse au siège de Mvola à Ankorondrano, les responsables de la société ont présenté leurs nouvelles orientations. « Sur les deux dernières années, Mvola a été victime de son propre succès. Nous avons grandi plus vite que ce qui était prévu, le marché s’est considérablement développé », a affirmé Alexandre Castel, CEO de la société. Selon les chiffres communiqués par l’entreprise, près de 4 millions de personnes utilisent Mvola et plus de 60 000 cashpoints maillent le territoire. Plus de 50 000 marchands acceptent également les paiements via ce service. Les paiements marchands occupent désormais une place centrale dans la stratégie de l’entreprise, sur un marché marqué par une forte progression des transactions. « L’enjeu est de rendre plus simple et plus attractif au quotidien le service de paiement marchand de Mvola. Pour le client, le principe est désormais clair: 0 frais lors d’un paiement auprès d’un marchand Mvola. Les frais sont pris en charge par le marchand. Pour les commerçants, cette évolution permet de proposer à leurs clients un moyen de paiement sans frais et s’accompagne aussi d’avantages dédiés », a expliqué Alexandre Castel. Parmi ces avantages, la société annonce trois retraits gratuits par semaine pour les commerçants, jusqu’à 250 000 ariary par retrait. Le paiement marchand constitue ainsi un axe de développement pour les opérateurs de mobile money. Plus largement, selon les chiffres de l’International Finance Corporation (IFC), la valeur des transactions effectuées par téléphone portable a doublé entre 2021 et 2023. Les données de la Coordination nationale de la finance inclusive (CNFI) illustrent également cette progression : en 2023, 342 millions de transactions ont représenté un montant total de 38 161 milliards d’ariary. Entre 2021 et 2023, le nombre de comptes actifs a augmenté de 48 %. Dynamique mondiale Le mobile money et le mobile banking prennent une place croissante dans les pratiques financières à Madagascar. Dans un pays où une grande partie de la population vit en milieu rural et où les contraintes logistiques restent importantes, le téléphone portable facilite l’accès aux services financiers. Le taux de bancarisation traditionnel se situe autour de 18 % de la population, selon les statistiques de la Banky Foibe, tandis que le mobile money dépasse les 10 millions de comptes actifs, selon l’IFC. Ces indicateurs mesurent toutefois des réalités différentes : le nombre de comptes ne correspond pas nécessairement au nombre d’utilisateurs, une même personne pouvant en détenir plusieurs. Cette expansion s’inscrit dans une dynamique mondiale. D’après le rapport de l’Association mondiale des opérateurs de téléphonie (GSMA) cité, la valeur des transactions d’argent mobile a dépassé 2 100 milliards de dollars en 2025. Alors qu’il avait fallu vingt ans pour atteindre les 1 000 milliards de dollars, ce montant a doublé en seulement quatre ans. Le nombre de comptes enregistrés atteint, quant à lui, 2,3 milliards. Selon la plateforme Digital Virgo, « cette accélération montre que la valeur des transactions augmente désormais plus rapidement que leur volume, signe évident que les utilisateurs s’engagent dans des activités financières plus approfondies et plus complexes ». À Madagascar, les opérateurs cherchent à accompagner cette évolution en développant de nouveaux usages, notamment le paiement auprès des commerçants. Itamara Otton

mg.title: APRÈS BAC - Les nouvelles séries alignées aux études supérieures
mg.description: Des étudiants de l’université d’Antananarivo lors du Salon de l’étudiant à Ankatso, au mois d’août. Les nouvelles séries L, S et OSE ont été pensées en cohérence avec l’enseignement supérieur, selon les informations recueillies. « Elles facilitent l’accès aux études supérieures », a indiqué le Pr Angelo Raherinirina, directeur général de l’Enseignement supérieur auprès du ministère de l’Enseignement supérieur et de la Recherche scientifique, hier. Les études supérieures se répartissent en trois grands domaines. Le lycée a été aligné en conséquence. Ainsi, Sciences et technologie pour la série scientifique, Sciences et sociétés pour la série Organisation-Société et Économie, et Sciences humaines et lettres pour la série Littéraire. « Avec les anciennes séries, les bacheliers avaient de la difficulté dans leur choix. Les candidats de la série A2, qui composent, par exemple, les 60 % des candidats, ne sont ni série scientifique ni série littéraire», poursuit la source. Le nouveau programme d’enseignement appliqué en parallèle avec ces nouvelles séries apporte, par ailleurs, des connaissances transversales nécessaires à l’accès aux universités. Les études supérieures sont structurées dans cette logique, et leurs critères ont été adaptés. Concrètement, un bachelier de la série S est orienté vers les parcours scientifiques et technologiques comme la Médecine, les Sciences, l’Agronomie, ou encore les filières des Écoles polytechniques. La série L prépare aux sciences humaines et aux lettres, comme les études de langue, l’Histoire, la Géographie, l’Anthropologie, la Philosophie. La série OSE prépare aux sciences et sociétés, comme les filières Gestion, Économie, Sociologie. Cette organisation concerne aussi les études à l’étranger. « Elle suit le système international, qui met en avant l’orientation par spécialité. Pour les bacheliers, cela facilite le choix de la spécialité et des options d’études hors du pays », explique ce responsable. L’orientation par spécialité devient ainsi le fil conducteur, du lycée aux études supérieures. Miangaly Ralitera

Un chiffre qui a visiblement marqué les esprits, puisque l’établissement a choisi d’en faire sa nouvelle doctrine. Jeudi 24 septembre 2026, le ton était donné dès la rentrée : ici, on n’attend plus l’emploi, […] L’article Yaoundé II-Soa : l’université mise tout sur l’entrepreneuriat étudiant est apparu en premier sur 237online.com .

cm.title: À Soa, fabriquer des patrons plutôt que distribuer des slogans
cm.description: L’Université de Yaoundé II-Soa met en avant l’entrepreneuriat dans sa préparation académique, selon un article publié le 2 octobre par Cameroon Tribune.

cm.title: Rougeole–rubéole : six millions d’enfants à atteindre en cinq jours
cm.description: Le Cameroun annonce une campagne nationale de vaccination contre la rougeole et la rubéole du 14 au 18 octobre. Environ six millions d’enfants âgés de 9 à 59 mois sont ciblés.

cm.title: Cacao à 2 600 FCFA : le record qui doit encore entrer dans la poche du planteur
cm.description: Le kilogramme de fèves de cacao s’est négocié jusqu’à 2 600 FCFA en fin de campagne, un niveau présenté comme record par Investir au Cameroun le 2 octobre.

cm.title: Péages automatiques : 3,1 milliards d’avances encore portés par Fayat
cm.description: Fayat indique porter encore environ 3,1 milliards de FCFA de prêts et avances nets sur Tollcam, société impliquée dans le partenariat public-privé de 14 postes de péage automatiques.

cm.title: Razel Cameroun : une perte de 12,3 milliards qui dépasse le simple mauvais chantier
cm.description: Razel-Bec a indiqué que sa filiale camerounaise avait enregistré en 2025 une perte de 12,3 milliards de FCFA pour un chiffre d’affaires de 28,4 milliards, selon Investir au Cameroun.

cm.title: Camrail : 300 millions de pertes chez l’actionnaire qui tient les commandes
cm.description: La Société camerounaise de chemin de fer, présentée comme l’actionnaire majoritaire de Camrail, aurait cumulé près de 300 millions de FCFA de pertes depuis 2019, selon une publication du 2 octobre.

cm.title: UNICS convoque ses actionnaires face à l’urgence du capital
cm.description: Les actionnaires d’UNICS sont convoqués le 7 octobre pour examiner une recapitalisation, dans un contexte de difficultés financières et de tutelle prudentielle évoqué par EcoMatin.

cm.title: Le crédit franchit 7 000 milliards, mais qui finance-t-il vraiment ?
cm.description: À fin juin 2026, les crédits bancaires au Cameroun s’élevaient à 7 041,2 milliards de FCFA, soit 723 milliards de plus qu’un an auparavant. La progression de 11,4 % est notamment soutenue par les prêts à moyen terme.
